Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing questionnaire — initial submission

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Attached is the procurement team's detailed sizing questionnaire for Dedicated capacity. We're trying to lock month-by-month committed vGPU lanes for H1 2027 and need Redwood's recommended GPU mix and throughput guidance to finalize our internal CAPEX request.

Key asks in the sheet: target token throughput per second for our conversational use case (75% of traffic), tail latency (95th pct target), and a recommended committed/burst split so we can size our reserved budget.

Can you confirm a timeline for a formal response? We ideally need the workbook back by 25 Nov to hit our internal procurement deadlines.

Attachments: datasilo_rfp_questionnaire_v1.xlsx (questionnaire)

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing questionnaire — initial submission

Kevin —

Thanks for the questionnaire and the deadline heads-up. I've started a draft in the attached workbook (datasilo_commitment_workbook_v2.xlsx) with our initial assumptions and a couple of clarifying items on page 2. High-level notes up front:

- For a conversational workload with 75% generation traffic, a mixed pool of H100 (inference-optimized 80GB) and A100 80GB with aggressive KV cache and prefix caching typically gives the best cost/latency tradeoffs.
- We recommend specifying a 70/30 committed split (70% of expected sustained throughput in reserved lanes, 30% as burst) for your initial 12-month runway; that reduces commit cost but preserves headroom for spikes.
- Tail latency: to hit 95th percentile <= 220ms for short-turn chat (avg sequence 120 tokens) we recommend conservative batch size 1–2 for H100 and allow batching to 4 on A100 for streaming-heavy flows.

Questions we have inline in the workbook: workload seasonality (month-over-month % variance), acceptable tail latency SLAs for non-chat inference (e.g., embeddings batch jobs), and whether you can route lower-priority background calls to an unreserved pool.

Connor and Aditya — looping you in for kernel-fit comments and to validate packing numbers. Connor: can you run the workbook's three example profiles (low/med/high concurrent conversations) through the kernel-fit script and add the per-GPU token/s and slot counts to the CSV? Aditya: please confirm expected pricing tiers and any available early-commit discounts we should propose in the workbook.

I'll aim to turn this into a final reply to Kevin on or before 25 Nov with the attached kernel-fit notes and throughput matrix.

Best,

Subject: INTERNAL: Datasilo — kernel fit and throughput estimates (action)

Connor / Aditya —

Quick internal note before you run numbers: DataSilo's sample profile in the questionnaire assumes 40k peak concurrent chat sessions, median seq 120 tokens, 18 requests/sec per user during bursts. They called out a strict 95th pct latency target of 250ms for priority chat.

Action items:
1) Connor — run the three profiles in the workbook (low: 5k cc, med: 20k, high: 40k) through the kernel-fit pipeline. Please produce: tokens/sec per GPU, estimated sustained qps at target latency, and suggested batch/concurrency knobs for H100 vs A100. Put your CSV into the shared folder and attach here.
2) Aditya — confirm whether we can offer a 6% committed discount at 12-month term and 9% at 24-month term for Dedicated pools (this is pricing playbook quick-check; we can adjust with sales later). Also confirm if we should recommend quantized variants for the embeddings-heavy background jobs.

Connor — would appreciate a short note on risk/assumptions (kernel versions, instruction-fusion coverage) so we can call that out to DataSilo procurement.

Thanks,
Kim
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Datasilo — kernel fit and throughput estimates (action)

Kim / Aditya —

I ran the three profiles against our 2026.11 kernel build. Notes and highlights below; full numbers are in throughput_matrix_connor_20261122.csv attached.

Assumptions: model horizon is a ~7B param chat model (decoder-only), avg token compute ~0.42 ms on H100 80GB when using fused-attn kernels; A100 is ~0.65 ms per token under similar packing. We assumed KV cache hit 28% on warm prefixes.

Summary per GPU (sustained at 95th pct latency target):
- H100 80GB: ~1,150 tokens/sec sustained (batch 1–2, priority), supports ~9 concurrent chat sessions at median seq 120 before tail latency rises above 250ms.
- A100 80GB: ~750 tokens/sec sustained (batch 2–4), supports ~6 concurrent chat sessions at same conditions.

Packing recommendations for DataSilo:
- For the medium profile (20k cc) with 70/30 committed/burst split, suggested committed pool = 1,600 H100-equivalent tokens/sec capacity. Practically that maps to 14 H100 + 8 A100 in a mixed pool (place H100s on low-latency lanes, A100s on secondary lanes for cost efficiency).
- For the high profile (40k cc), recommend staging an initial committed pool to cover ~28k sustained tokens/sec and leave 20% headroom via burst lanes and autoscaling. That maps to 28 H100 + 16 A100 as an initial commit.

Risks / assumptions:
- These numbers assume current kernel fusion levels and our recent batching heuristics. If kernel updates change GEMM tiling or attention fusion, per-token MS could shift ~±12%.
- We recommended enabling prefix/KV caching for chat front-ends and a dedicated caching tier. That reduces effective compute by ~18–25% on repeated prompts and materially reduces committed capacity needs.

I've attached the CSV and a short PDF with kernel-fit commentary for inclusion in the workbook.

Attachments: throughput_matrix_connor_20261122.csv, kernel-fitment-notes-kpark.pdf

Connor

Subject: Final: Dedicated commitment scenarios, recommended GPU mix, and workbook (DataSilo)

Kevin / Sandra —

Appended is our consolidated response to your questionnaire and the commitment workbook you requested. Highlights and recommended ask for procurement:

1) Recommended committed/burst strategy (12 month):
   - Start with a 70% committed / 30% burst allocation. For your medium operating profile (20k concurrent chats) we recommend an initial committed pool sized for ~1,600 H100-equivalent sustained tokens/sec.
   - This maps to a mixed pool of 14 H100 + 8 A100 for the committed lanes, with the remainder of burst capacity handled by autoscaling GPU instances in the same region.

2) Tail latency and packing guidance:
   - Target 95th pct <= 220–250ms for chat when batching is kept small (1–2 for H100). A100 lanes can be used at slightly larger batch sizes for cost-efficiency on non-interactive flows.

3) Cost and term recommendations:
   - We can offer a 6% committed discount on top of list pricing for a 12-month Dedicated commitment; a 9% discount for a 24-month commitment. These are initial pricing notes and can be formalized in a commercial SOW.

4) Operational recommendations:
   - Enable prefix/KV caching for the chat front-end to reduce effective compute load (~18–25% savings).
   - Keep a dedicated small instance pool for background embeddings/ETL (quantized variants suggested).
   - Include a 20% burst buffer in your procurement plan to handle regional traffic spikes and release gating during model rollouts.

Attached: datasilo_commitment_workbook_v2.xlsx (filled answers + three scenarios), throughput_matrix_connor_20261122.csv (per-GPU tokens/sec and slot counts), kernel-fitment-notes-kpark.pdf (assumptions and risk items).

Next steps: if this aligns with your procurement timeline we'll prepare a formal SOW + pricing schedule and a short tech validation call with Connor to walk the datasheet. Can you confirm whether 25 Nov meets your internal deadline or if you need an earlier review?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call Thurs or Fri to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Kimberly Park
